crime.value: Bank robbery during business hours; central question: will the robber escape with hostage and money, or will authorities intercept him?
crime.quote: two people arrived...A tall slender man in a windbreaker followed her closely...he said softly, 'but be careful, very, very careful.' He pushed the black bag across the counter top.

victim.value: Marge Elliot, bank teller—a dutiful suburban housewife trapped between domestic obligations and her own suppressed desires, making her psychologically vulnerable to the robber's manipulation.
victim.quote: Marge was hungry...too tired to start the annual argument about the parents' show...After fourteen years no woman got excited.

culprit_and_motive.value: The robber, a Korean War veteran escaping a suffocating marriage and bourgeois entrapment. Motive: violent rebellion against domestic servitude and societal conformity; he seeks freedom through crime and explicitly states he will not be captured alive.
culprit_and_motive.quote: I had to get out of it...I don't know. Maybe I did love her, maybe I still do...Either I make it with the money, or they kill me. But they won't catch me!

resolution.value: The robber is killed in a police shootout after being tracked via Marge's abandoned watch. Marge is rescued but psychologically transformed—no longer the compliant housewife. She rejects Warren's comfort and the promise of returning to 'normal.'
resolution.quote: There was a distant, lost sound of a siren...rapid, faint reports of guns firing...over the cliff...She jerked away from him and buried her face in the pillow, where her abductor's head had rested.

investigator.value: Marge Elliot herself—the victim-witness whose internal perspective dominates the narrative. She experiences the crime as both captive and reluctant confidante, gradually recognizing uncomfortable truths about her own life.
investigator.quote: It was as if she were coming out from a deep dream, only now being consciously in control of her actions...Why hadn't she screamed in the lot?
